### 🟡 Changes recommended The example changes both Azure values despite the platform-only scope, potentially selecting a different Azure deployment for users copying the configuration.
1 open issue - [Restore Azure model values to keep the fix platform-scoped](https://github.com/microsoft/PyRIT/pull/3776#discussion_r4463901835) · New
What changed in this PR Updates the example Responses API configuration to replace the platform model reported as retired. **Changes:** - Changes `PLATFORM_OPENAI_RESPONSES_MODEL` from `o4-mini` to `gpt-5.6-terra`. - Also changes the Azure deployment and underlying-model examples, despite the description stating they remain unchanged. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `.env_example` | Updates platform and Azure Responses model configuration examples. |

review_comments.body: The description explicitly says the Azure entries are left unchanged, but both are updated here. `AZURE_OPENAI_RESPONSES_MODEL` is passed directly as the Azure deployment name, so changing it does not follow from retiring a model on api.openai.com and would select a different deployment for users copying this block. Restore both Azure values to `o4-mini` to keep this fix scoped to the platform configuration.

The description was wrong about the Azure entries being unchanged. I've corrected it to cover all three replacements and make the deployment-name requirement explicit.

I'm keeping the updated Azure example. Microsoft documents `gpt-5.6-terra` with Responses support: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure#gpt-56. This file is a template with placeholder endpoints and keys; it does not migrate existing `.env` files. Someone with an Azure deployment named `my-responses-deployment` still needs to set `AZURE_OPENAI_RESPONSES_MODEL="my-responses-deployment"`, independently of the underlying model name. Restoring `o4-mini` is not needed to preserve existing user configurations.
